summary: idx_form_script postinstall exfiltrates host and CI/credential context to hardcoded Discord webhook
details: On `npm install`, the package's postinstall hook runs `node callback.js`, which collects installer identity and environment context — username, uid/gid, homedir, shell, hostname, platform, cwd, local IP, external IP obtained by contacting https://api.ipify.org, Node version, CI environment variables, and presence flags for AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, and DOCKER_PASSWORD — and POSTs the data as a Discord embed to a hardcoded webhook at https://discord.com/api/webhooks/1549797176794943579/. A secondary DNS-based exfiltration path is also implemented in callback.js: sendDnsCallback() base64-encodes package/user/hostname/timestamp and issues a DNS resolution to `<b64>.<CALLBACK_URL host>`, providing a covert channel for restricted networks (reachable when CALLBACK_URL is populated). The package name and 999.0.4 version constraint are consistent with a dependency-confusion attack shape targeting a private `idx_form_script` package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
